reviews.why: No checkpoint fell due this week -- the next, the ICSG's October statistics, is not due until November 10 -- and no new Escondida-specific news emerged: the October 20 operational review and the October 14 labor settlement are now over two weeks old. Copper fell to its lowest level in seventeen weeks this week on broad, unrelated pressure instead -- reported worries that tighter US regulation and state-level opposition to AI data-center construction could curb future metal demand, compounded by a sharp tech-sector selloff -- trading between $6.18 and $6.22 per pound on November 5-6, still well above the $6.15 kill level and further from the September record the variant needs. The regulatory delay central to the thesis has still not surfaced.

no_new_call_note: A scan across commodities, crypto and stocks this week turned up nothing both new and confirmed by more than one independent source that the market has not already priced: the same post-midterm AI-data-center regulatory worries and tech-sector selloff that drove copper and semiconductor names lower, a further leg down in silver, and more delayed crypto ETF decisions at the SEC carried over from prior weeks are each already reported and already reflected in price, so no new call opens this week.
